verdicts.verdict_one_line: Its reasoning block states prediction 'yes' at 0.55 and every reasoning step resolves to 'uncertain' or 'neutral', yet the forecast answers 'no' at 0.70 - a 0.0017 percentage-point margin on a wholly invented -0.5 estimate is converted into the packet's most confident claim, and it declares metric_match 'direct' while conceding magnitude support is 'unsupported'.

ranking_rationale: The separator at the top was whether a trace did question-specific work and then kept its confidence inside the limits it had just declared: hgf explicitly re-tested each inherited causal path and marked the rate-cut premise reversed against dated sources, and it, factor_memory and structure_memory all held their mass near uniform after conceding magnitude support was insufficient. The bottom three all crossed a precise numeric boundary on no quantity at all - principle_memory by assuming an unevidenced end to QT, structured_reasoning by re-reading its own dominant down-driver as an up-driver, and case_memory by turning a 0.0017pp gap between an invented -0.5 and the -0.498315 threshold into 70 percent confidence while its reasoning block still said 'yes'.
shared_evidence_note: The disagreement is not evidentiary - both banks are title-only snippets with no balance-sheet quantities, and E0 and E1 share the decisive QT and May-2025 rate-hold items - so the yes/no split traces entirely to how each method handled the same admitted magnitude gap, specifically whether its fabricated central estimate happened to land above or below -0.498315.
